hook: Things that are NORMAL as uni students
caption:
What we see on social media is NOT the case for 99% of us, and sometimes they are straight up lies ⬇️

Despite getting mostly 100s across all my assignments, I would be lying if I said I didn't feel overwhelmed, never struggled to understand the material, and never got low grades

School is hard. You're not behind, you're normal!!

It's important to understand that if you expect to always get good grades, have lots of free time, excel at your hobbies, and have the time to make genuine friends, you're literally asking for perfection.

We don't have to, and won't be perfect.

But we can try.

And we are trying. We're trying everyday to continue improving.

That is what matters!!!

I hope this message found you when you needed.

For what it's worth, I'm genuinely proud of you. I know how hard school can be.

Good luck, you got this 💛

I'm currently building a system for students to maximize grades while minimizing study time, if that interests you, follow along!

I'll see you tomorrow 💛

  - Share a specific and honest example from your own experience that shows you are not perfect either

hook: If you're between 19-22, in Uni, worrying if you're in the wrong major and don't know what the future looks like…
caption:
Feeling lost and don't know what to do with your life? Here's what changed everything for me ⬇️

I took a year off school to play professional badminton, thinking it was my purpose in life

After 6 months, I quit.

I was completely lost, and terrified of being "left behind"

If you're anything like me, you were probably told you have to "find yourself", "go find your purpose"

This just made me more scared… "I can't start over, it's too late", "how do I find myself?"

It's finally in the last few months that I feel I've found my purpose, like I'm right where I'm supposed to be

Here are some things you need to realize:

1️⃣ You can't find yourself if you don't go exploring.

The more things you try, the better you'll understand yourself. You can't just "think" your way into finding yourself.

2️⃣ You have to copy others

This follows a famous Japanese philosophy called "Shu-Ha-Ri".
Right now you are probably trying to "innovate" a purpose, something completely unique to you. But the truth is, purpose comes from the world around us. if you copy the mindsets of people you admire and the activities they do, then at the end of all this copying, you will find yourself.

3️⃣ STOP looking 10 years down the line

We as humans are dynamic creatures, which means our passions and interests will change over time. If you thought you wanted to be a twitch streamer when you were 12, you probably have different desires now. Looking 10 years down the line might overwhelm you with commitment like it did for me.

4️⃣ Remove societal expectations

Don't fall into the trap of picking careers based off of the "impact" it has on the world or how well it's respected like I did. The world wouldn't be better if Goggins was a doctor, or if Marcus Aurelius was a scientist. Impact comes from YOU, not your career.

Remember this: You don't need to change the world, you just need to bloom where you're planted.

If no one else is going to tell you, then for what it's worth, I think you're doing great. You're not behind, you're just in your own story. I'm proud of you. 💛

Follow for more daily reminders and thoughts like this! I'll see you tomorrow💛

3 reasons why traveling in your late 20s isn’t fun anymore

(read caption)
caption:
I don’t really enjoy traveling as much as I did in my early 20s. And it’s taken me a while to realize that.

I’m 28, and I’ve traveled now to 27 countries (on track to hit 30 countries by 30!). In my early 20s, I loved traveling and even interned at an airline where I got free flights all summer.

But, as I’m getting older, I’m thinking more about how I prioritize my time, money and energy. And traveling doesn’t hit quite the same anymore.

Here are the 3 main reasons why (would love to hear if you resonate):

1. After a certain number of countries, the novelty starts to wear off. Big cities feel the same, outdoor hikes feel the same, and new places aren’t as exciting anymore.

2. I often travel without my fiancé or family, and even though the trip will be great, I really miss them. Is it really worth it to see so many places if they’re not there with me? I feel like I’m choosing between novelty/adventure vs rootedness/relationships.

3. The cost of traveling is not just money anymore. It’s the cost of messing up my sleep and health routines, missing the comforts of home, and the toll on my physical and emotional energy. I can’t do multiple layovers, red-eyes or budget airlines / hotels anymore.

Overall, I feel like I’ve traveled enough. Especially during this MBA program, often times I’m going to a different country every month and it’s exhausting. I’m losing the joy that I had.

I say this, and I still have a few trips planned, but I’m realizing that travel is not a big priority for me anymore. And that’s ok!

It’s so helpful for me now to have clarity about what does make me feel fulfilled and what I think is a good use of my time, money and energy.

Would love to hear what you think!
notes:

An honest and slightly unpopular opinions are highly effective at driving comments and discussion

It also goes against the usual highlight reel of travel content, and the promise of "3 reasons" makes viewers curious enough to read the full explanation

I don’t want a life that only looks successful. I want a life that feels successful.

A life where my time is valued more than my title.

Where my joy is richer than any paycheck.

Where I can breathe deeply, love fully, and sleep peacefully.

Because at the end of the day, no one remembers your job title. They remember how you made them feel. And you remember whether you were truly happy.

startea coming one arter anotner.

15 TRAVEL HACKS THAT ACTUALLY SAVE YOU MONEY 🌍✈️

1. Be flexible with dates

Flying mid-week or at odd hours is often way cheaper. Flexibility is currency.

2. Let the destination choose you

Search “Anywhere” from your city. The cheapest flight might change your whole plan.

3. Track prices, don’t rush

Set price alerts and wait. Most people overpay because they book emotionally.

4. Pack carry-on only

No baggage fees, no waiting, no stress. Pack smart and do laundry on the road.

5. Book flights in incognito

Avoid price jumps from repeated searches. Small trick, real difference.

6. Stay where locals stay

Hostels, guesthouses, and private rooms are cheaper and more social than hotels.

7. Slow travel

Fewer flights, longer stays = lower costs and better experiences.

8. Travel off-season

Same places, fewer crowds, half the price. Shoulder season is elite.

9. Use public transport

Buses and metros save money and show you the real city.

10. Eat local, not tourist food

If there’s no English menu, you’re in the right place—and paying less.

11. Withdraw cash wisely

Avoid airport exchanges. Use ATMs and low-fee cards instead.

12. Book accommodation with kitchens

Cooking a few meals saves more than you think.

13. Take overnight transport

Night buses or trains save you a night of accommodation.

14. Work or volunteer while traveling

Hostels, farms, or cafes often offer free stays for a few hours of work.

💡 Bonus: With the code NOA200, you get $10 off your Worldpackers membership.

15. Don’t move too fast

Constant movement is expensive. Staying put saves money and energy.

caption:
If I could go back, I’d start here.

If you’re between 25–35, start these 11 habits before it’s too late.

Simple. Grounded. Real.

The kind of habits that, over time, create peace, confidence, and freedom.

✨ Save this. Your future self will thank you.

1. When in doubt – move your body.

Go for a walk, dance in the bathroom, stretch, shake… move that energy. It will shift your state and bring clarity.

2. Morning self-care: non-negotiable.

Even 10 minutes. Prayer, stretching, sitting still with your thoughts, setting intention. It’s the difference between reacting to your day and creating it.

3. Master your mindset.

Thoughts become beliefs.

Beliefs become behaviors.

If you don’t learn to control your mind, it will control you.

4. Protect your energy (aka boundaries).

Took me forever to learn this. The more you say no to what doesn’t serve you, the more room you have for what does.

5. Discipline (I know, I know).

I used to think it was restrictive.

Turns out it’s the opposite.

Discipline is what gives you the freedom to actually do what you want.

6. Be intentional with your screen time.

First hour of the day and last hour before bed, keep them phone-free. Notice how much calmer you feel.

7. Doing things that scare you a little.

New cities. New hobbies. Saying yes when you’d usually say no. You find out who you are when you step outside what’s familiar.

8. Talking to yourself like someone you love. Would you talk to your best friend the way you talk to yourself? Yeah. That’s the work.

9. Get into gratitude practice.

It’s the best thing you can do for yourself.

I’m not talking about toxic positivity, I’m talking about noticing the small moments that actually shape your life.

Urine that sits in your bladder for too long creates a breeding ground for bacteria, which increases your risk of urinary tract infections and other bladder problems.

Mouth breathing can worsen sleep quality, dry your mouth, and contribute to snoring. Persistent snoring is also linked to higher blood pressure.

3️⃣ Sitting with poor posture for too long

Hunching over for hours strains your back and neck, causing pain, stiffness, and potential long term issues.

4️⃣ Sitting on the toilet for too long

Sitting too long puts extra pressure on your veins in that area, which can lead to hemorrhoids.

5️⃣ Constantly touching your face

Your hands pick up bacteria all day, and touching your face spreads it which can lead to skin irritation and acne.

6️⃣ Wearing tight headphones for hours

Tight headphones trap heat and sweat in your ears, which can irritate the skin and lead to infections.

7️⃣ Eating too fast

Eating too quickly can make you overeat and feel bloated because your brain hasn’t had time to realize you’re full.

9️⃣ Using very hot showers too often

Hot water removes the protective oils on your skin, causing dryness, irritation, and sometimes itchiness.

hook: 13 things that every traveler will regret not knowing
caption:
Save these important details for your next trip ✈️

1. The carry-on limit for liquid items is 100ml.

2. If you miss the first leg of your connecting flight, the rest of the flight is automatically canceled.

3. If there’s anything of value (e.g., diamond ring, camera, grad certificate), never check it in. Airlines lose luggage every day.

4. There are different charging ports in different parts of the world - you will need a universal charger.

5. The worst place to change your foreign currency is the airport.

6. Make sure your passport has enough pages and is valid for >6 months always.

7. The most annoying way to waste your time at the airport is by not having a pen. Keep one with you at all times.

8. Most countries will not let you enter their territory without having a return ticket. If you must buy a one-way ticket, get a second one-way ticket for your return.

9. You should take pictures of your passport, visas, and travel insurance and email them to yourself in case you lose them on a trip.

10. Speaking of travel insurance, you will definitely be needing it. Don’t forget to buy.

11. If you do not turn off your cellular data before you land in a new country, you may be hit with roaming charges.

hook: “Will I be rich as a nurse?”
caption:
A lot of people ask me,

“How much do you earn as a nurse?”

And while I don’t mind answering, the truth is… it’s never just about the paycheck.

Nursing makes you rich in so many ways that go beyond salary:

1. Compassion

You learn to care deeply — for strangers, for families, for people going through the hardest moments of their lives. Compassion becomes second nature, and that’s a kind of wealth not everyone gets to develop.

2. Community

Nurses don’t just work together — we rely on each other. You gain a second family in your coworkers, mentors, and even patients who leave an impact on you.

3. Health

You become more aware of your own well-being. You understand prevention, you advocate for yourself, and you make choices that support a healthier lifestyle.

4. Experiences

Every shift teaches you something new. You witness life, loss, recovery, resilience — and those moments shape you in ways that no classroom ever could.

5. Faith

Not necessarily religious faith — but faith in people, in second chances, in healing, in timing. You start believing that small acts can create big change.

6. Discipline

Waking up early, long shifts, constant learning, managing stress — nursing builds discipline that carries over into every area of your life.

7. Purpose

This is the deepest kind of wealth. At the end of the day, you know your work matters. You know you’re part of someone’s story, someone’s healing, someone’s hope.

So yes — nursing can give you financial stability.

But it also makes you rich in ways that money can’t measure.

If you are interested to be a nurse in the US, comment the word “NCLEX” and I can help you get started.

You start missing home, questioning your choices, and wondering if this move was really right. (Spoiler; you will always be questioning yourself)

Stage 5: The Anxiety Phase

Life abroad isn’t all glamour; paperwork, appointments, and language barriers can hit hard. Your nervous system might be in overdrive for a while.

Stage 6: The Social Reset Phase

You meet tons of new people at first, but eventually you figure out who truly clicks and who drifts away.

Stage 7: The “I am actually thriving” Phase

Around six months in, you finally feel at home, find your people, and realize this new life is yours to shape.

Lastly for this part, an authentic emotion is also very much necessary.

EXPLOSION:

A significant moment where an event/decision brings you from this struggle to where you are now.

For Makayla, this was her being a “petty bitch” and deciding to drop her classes for next semester to prove him wrong and clap back at men.

This is where you dive in to talk more specifically to your niche. You’ve already gained the attention of people up until this point, so now you can call out to your niche more specifically.

This is the most important part to convert viewers to followers. You’ve earned their attention, now you have to earn their trust.

So form that connection by stating a shared goal.

To finish the video off, just add a classic call to action. Nothing fancy, just telling the viewer what they will get from following you and taking action.

I have no friends, I live alone, and I'm choosing to be single. The most common question I get asked is why. Surely there was something that made you this way, right? So hi, my name's Lana. I grew up on welfare and subsidized housing with a dad who abused my mom. When I say we had nothing, I truly mean we had nothing except the earwigs that were all over that house. My dad would leave us 10 days a month without any money. And my mom would try to find work, but not only could she not find work because of a gap on her resume, she also couldn't afford childcare. So my mom did what she thought was best for us and sacrificed her own happiness, allowing my father back into our lives just so we could afford food. I don't know why, but I was never a naive child and I always was aware of what was going on. Such a core memory of my childhood was seeing a full happy family for the first time. As a young child, you can truly only know what you've been shown. So when I saw that other kid outside of school with her parents, I remember thinking, wow, they truly must be the chosen one. Shortly after that day, my dad came back with so many promises like he always had. But something felt different this time. He took my mom, my sister, and I to Best Buy and he bought us an Xbox. Listen, for a family rationing $30 for two weeks at a time. An Xbox felt like a Lamborghini. My sister and I played on the Xbox that night. While my mom and dad sat on the couch happily walking. script: I had everything a nice Chinese boy was supposed to be happy with. Top engineering degree, six-figure job, even a girlfriend who treated me right. And a week later, my relationship fell apart. While numbing my heartbreak with alcohol and video games, I decided I had enough. So I threw myself into the gym, losing 20 pounds and still feeling empty. I tried dating apps, got played, and deleted them for good. Then came side hustle after side hustle, which all failed. Until finally, I picked up a camera and just started recording my life. For the first time ever, a flame lit up inside of me. Maybe because for once, it wasn't on anyone else's checklist. And even before I had 100 followers, I wrote in my journal that I quit my job to chase this feeling. I spent all of my free time learning how to get better, and a month later, I quit my job to do content full-time. Just to grind day after day, seeing no results. But the truth is, the success just made me depressed. I genuinely considered ending my life. And as bad as that sounds, rock bottom was the best thing that ever happened to me. caption:
Exactly 21 years ago, my parents chose the unthinkable - to leave behind their comfortable middle-class life in Singapore and move our family to Brisbane, Australia.

My brother and I were already studying in good schools, we were financially stable and had extended family around. They didn’t know anyone in Brisbane and would even have to run a business to be granted residency. So why?

Looking back, my parents sensed that doing the status quo - pushing their kids to study hard, come first in class, get into the best university and be miserable their whole childhood - just didn’t seem quite right. Surely they thought there must be a different way to life where their kids could have better opportunities and the space to dream of their future beyond conforming to fit a mould in society.

So for years they adopted the immigrant life and started from nothing- sold vegemite sandwiches, learned how to cook fish and chips, worked the graveyard shift at the post office, all so we could have a better future.

20 years later, I realise my parents were teaching me the meaning of hard work, never settling for less. I’ve achieved things I wouldn’t have dreamed of if my parents hadn’t given up their comfortable lives. I practice in a suburb in Sydney where there are lots of Asian immigrants like me. As a bilingual English and Mandarin speaking orthodontist, I get to connect with lots of patients and their families with similar backgrounds and experiences, and help them understand their dental and orthodontic health in a way that comforts and reassures them.

I’m forever grateful to my parents for taking that risk.

Follow [@drjessyeo.ortho](https://www.instagram.com/drjessyeo.ortho/) for more.

#orthodontist #sydney #australia #immigrantstories

As someone who’s in one of the healthiest relationships I’ve ever been in, I thought I’d share some tips on what makes our relationship great! And things that I continue to learn along the way :)

This one is about loving their core traits in ALL contexts. You can love a quality in one context, then dislike that same exact quality you said you loved, just cuz the context has changed. That’s not love that’s just convenience for you.

script: You can't love someone for something and then get upset at them for the same exact quality. Let me explain. My girlfriend is a perfectionist. And honestly, it's one of the things that I love most about her. She holds herself to a high standard and everything she does is thoughtful, intentional, and just always executed to perfection. And it's part of what makes her feel so special to me. But the other day, she asked me to help her with a video and we started doing take after take after take. And I'm not going to lie, I started to get irritated. And I know that she could feel it too because I'm not exactly subtle when I'm annoyed. But mid-shoot, I caught myself. This is the same perfectionism that I admire when she plans an incredible trip or makes me the perfect meal or writes me the perfect card. So why would I love that quality only when it benefits me but get frustrated when it requires a little bit of patience? That's not how it works. And that's not fair to her. So I took a deep breath and I told her, don't worry about me. I'm just a little irritable right now. We can take as many takes as you'd like. So here's the takeaway. You can't pick and choose when to love someone's core traits. If you celebrate them in one context, you have to learn to accept them in others as well. Otherwise, it's not really love.
